body.heading: Forgotten goals are not failed goals
paragraphs: Ask someone about a goal they set in January and you will often see a small startle: they had simply stopped thinking about it. The goal did not lose an argument. It just left the room, crowded out by everything louder.
Visibility is the fix, and it is almost embarrassingly simple: a goal written where your eyes land every day stays gently present without any effort of remembering.

body.heading: One sentence, well placed
paragraphs: Write the goal as one short sentence in the present tense of effort: “I am learning Spanish, ten minutes a day.” Not the dream version, not a paragraph of motivation — just the goal and its rhythm, plain enough to read in one glance.

Place it where your eyes already go: the bathroom mirror, the lock screen, the first page of the notebook, the fridge door. One place is enough; plastering it everywhere turns it into wallpaper your eyes skip.

body.heading: Let the sentence retire gracefully
paragraphs: When the goal changes shape — smaller, slower, different — rewrite the sentence. The card on the mirror should always describe the current plan, not preserve an old one as an accusation.
And when a goal is complete or consciously released, take the sentence down with a small moment of thanks. Goals are allowed to end. The space on the mirror is for the living ones.

takeaway: One sentence, one well-chosen spot — let your eyes keep the goal in the room.
